big-news.text: The government wants a 16-year age limit for TikTok, Snapchat and Roblox, and possibly YouTube. The bill should reach the Storting by the end of the year and take effect next year.
This year's TV-aksjonen raised 251 million kroner for the Norwegian Refugee Council.
AUF, Labour's youth wing, picked 28-year-old Fawzi Warsame from Oslo as its new leader and voted to keep saying no to the EU.

whats-changing.text: Most of the Storting wants kids born in December to get a kindergarten (barnehage) place by age one, but the government won't promise it for children born this year.
The new airports in Bodø and Mo i Rana are set to go over budget by billions, which could mean pricier plane tickets.

oslo.text: City commissioner Anita Leirvik North, from Høyre (the Conservatives), won't run for re-election. She's the one Labour accused of lying at the Røabadet pool hearing.
Labour is criticizing the city government's plan to sell Lokomotivverkstedet in Middelalderparken.
A reminder that almost the whole T-bane closes Nov 19–22.

be-aware.text: It's tyre-change season, and the authorities are asking people to check that their tyre shop is legit, because the busy season brings more illegal labour.
There are no weather warnings for Oslo, but northern Nordland and Troms have an orange warning for heavy rain.

fun-and-free.text: Top pick: We Do Festival opens with a free Bad Ritual concert at Factory Tøyen on Wednesday at 19:30.
Høststorm, the free wind concert by Barratt Due students, is tomorrow at 18:00. You need to grab a free ticket.
There's a free Sunday World concert with Cuerda Nova at Juret on Sunday at 19:00, with an open jam after.
